title: High-Capacity Hydrogen and Hydrogen Isotope Getters
description: Even small amounts of hydrogen can damage sensitive equipment over time. As hydrogen accumulates inside sealed environments, it can corrode metals, weaken structural materials, degrade electronic components, and, in some applications, create explosion hazards. Preventing that buildup is essential for maintaining the reliability and safety of many high-value systems. Hydrogen getters are materials built into sealed devices and systems to remove hydrogen before it can accumulate. Like a moisture absorber, they remove an unwanted gas. Instead of trapping water, however, they chemically react with hydrogen and lock it away permanently. Depending on the application, a getter may take the form of a pellet, coating, thin film, powder, or printable material. Many commercially available getters rely on zirconium-based materials that offer limited hydrogen storage capacity, require activation before use, or operate effectively only within a narrow temperature range. Some also depend on costly vacuum-deposition manufacturing processes that limit design flexibility. Los Alamos researchers have developed a new class of hydrogen getters designed to overcome these limitations. The materials capture hydrogen and its isotopes, including deuterium and tritium, across a broad range of operating conditions without requiring activation while offering significantly higher storage capacity and greater flexibility for manufacturing and product integration. Value Proposition Hydrogen can quietly build up inside sealed devices and industrial systems, shortening equipment life and creating safety risks. Los Alamos National Laboratory has developed a new class of high-capacity hydrogen getters that permanently remove hydrogen before it causes damage. Compared with conventional getters, this technology stores more hydrogen, operates across a wider range of conditions, and can be manufactured in multiple forms for easy integration into commercial products. Hydrogen uptake rate decreases as getter materials fill with hydrogen. Compared with a conventional getter (brown), the LANL high-capacity getter (green) maintains rapid hydrogen capture over a much larger storage capacity. Advantages Stores significantly more hydrogen than many conventional getter materials. Permanently removes hydrogen, improving long-term reliability in sealed systems. Operates across a broad temperature range without activation. Captures hydrogen even at pressures well below atmospheric levels. Selectively removes hydrogen in mixed-gas environments. Hydrogen uptake rates can be tailored to specific applications. Compatible with polymers and available as films, coatings, pellets, powders, strands, and printable pastes for flexible product integration. Reduces projected material and manufacturing costs compared with many zirconium-based getter technologies. Scalable manufacturing supports applications ranging from miniature electronics to large industrial systems. Technology Description The getter materials chemically react with hydrogen and its isotopes to form stable compounds that permanently lock the hydrogen inside the material, providing long-term protection for sealed devices and industrial equipment. The technology is based on a novel organic alkyne chemistry. Alkynes are carbon-containing molecules that readily react with hydrogen, allowing the material to store substantially more hydrogen than many conventional getter systems. Unlike many commercial getters, these materials operate without activation and continue to perform across a broad temperature range. They also selectively capture hydrogen in the presence of gases such as helium, nitrogen, argon, and methane, making them well suited for complex industrial and vacuum environments. The hydrogen capture rate can be tailored by adjusting the catalyst formulation for specific operating conditions. Hydrogen capture has also been demonstrated at pressures well below atmospheric conditions, expanding the range of potential applications. The materials are compatible with polymers and other common manufacturing materials, allowing them to be incorporated into films, coatings, pellets, powders, strands, adhesives, foams, and printable pastes. buyer: Rectorado de la Universitat Politècnica de València
title: Spain – Microelectronic machinery and apparatus and microsystems – Suministro de sistema de grabado mediante haz iónico (Ion beam Etching - IBE)
description: El equipo se destinará a la Infraestructura Científica y Técnica Singular (ICTS) MICRONANOFABS, red española de salas blancas de micro y nanofabricación integrada en el Mapa Nacional de ICTS del Ministerio competente en materia de ciencia, de la que forma parte la Infraestructura de Micro y Nano Fabricación del Centro de Tecnología Nanofotónica (NTC) de la Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV), junto con el Centro Nacional de Microelectrónica (CSIC) y la Central de Tecnología del ISOM (UPM). La instalación se ubicará en la Sala Blanca del edificio 8F del NTC-UPV. El Centro de Tecnología Nanofotónica desarrolla procesos de fabricación de dispositivos fotónicos integrados, biosensores, componentes de óptica integrada, dispositivos cuánticos, sistemas microelectromecánicos (MEMS), estructuras microfluídicas y sistemas nanofotónicos sobre una amplia variedad de materiales, incluyendo silicio, nitruro de silicio, vidrio, cuarzo, materiales III-V, materiales dieléctricos y estructuras híbridas. Como ICTS integrada en la red MICRONANOFABS, el NTC-UPV presta servicios de micro y nanofabricación a grupos de investigación nacionales e internacionales, así como a empresas, en el marco de proyectos competitivos, contratos de transferencia tecnológica y prestación de servicios avanzados. Esta condición de infraestructura singular de uso compartido obliga a mantener una dotación instrumental actualizada, robusta y de prestaciones acordes al estado del arte, que permita dar respuesta tanto a las líneas de investigación propias como a la demanda externa de la comunidad científica e industrial, en línea con los objetivos del PERTE Chip para el fortalecimiento de las capacidades nacionales de microelectrónica y fotónica. Muchos de los dispositivos que se fabrican en la infraestructura requieren procesos de grabado físico de elevada precisión sobre materiales para los que los procesos convencionales de grabado químico (húmedo) no proporcionan la calidad superficial, anisotropía o selectividad necesarias. Asimismo, la creciente complejidad de los dispositivos desarrollados exige disponer de procesos altamente reproducibles, con control preciso del ángulo de incidencia del haz, elevada estabilidad del proceso, automatización y monitorización continua.

title: Install C2F Campus Static Displays (Deterrence Park)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / MARKET SURVEY This is a SOURCES SOUGHT notice; a market survey for information only, to be used for preliminary planning purposes. This is NOT a request for quotes or proposals. The intent of this notice is to identify qualified, experienced, and interested offerors capable of performing the type of work as described herein for information and planning purposes. The information received will be utilized by the United States Air Force to facilitate the planning and decision-making process and will not be disclosed outside of the agency. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. Respondents will NOT be notified of the results of this sources sought. Respondents are not required to submit information in response to this announcement to participate in any future solicitation that may come as a result of the information received. In accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c)(2), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The 55th Contracting Squadron, Offutt Air Force Base, NE, is seeking information for the following items listed below: General: The purpose of this sources sought is to conduct Market Research in accordance with RFO Part 10, to secure professional Architect-Engineer (A-E) services to update and revise completed construction drawings, technical specifications, and cost estimates for Project SGBP 20-0077, Install C2F Campus Static Displays (Deterrence Park) at Building 1000, Offutt Air Force Base, Nebraska. This requirement consists of highly specialized professional site investigation, a physical survey to verify "as-is" field conditions left by a prior terminated contractor, and the re-engineering of the baseline design to isolate the primary missile deck as a standalone Base Bid. The selected firm must design a permanent geotechnical foundation solution to correct subgrade soil bearing capacity issues to safely support static display missile loads (130,000 lbs for the Trident II display and 36,294 lbs for the Minuteman I display), resolve precise utility and footing interferences (specifically Structure S-7 rim elevations and pipe P4), and perform a physical serviceability audit of leftover on-base construction materials to compile a formal Government-Furnished Property schedule. Please see the attached Statement of Work for more information. All project work and related services shall be performed IAW all terms, conditions, special contract requirements, specifications, attachments, technical exhibits and references and publications contained in the contract or incorporated by reference. All information is voluntary. The capabilities package should be complete and sufficiently detailed enough to allow the Government to determine the firm�s qualifications to perform the defined work. Your response should include the following information: Company Information Company name Address Point of contact Telephone and fax number E-mail address Website (if available) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code Unique Entity ID (UEI) Number Socio-Economic status (i.e., 8(a), HUBZone, women-owned, service-disabled veteran-owned, etc.) Experience and overview of your company, specifically demonstrating your firm's capability to legally and ethically build upon, modify, and apply a professional engineering seal to a proprietary baseline design package originally developed and sealed by a different firm of record. Responses to this sources sought announcement can be submitted to the 55th Contracting Squadron via e-mail to blaine.terry.2@us.af.mil by 12:00 PM Central Standard Time on 14 November 2026. IF A SOLICITATION IS ISSUED, IT WILL BE ANNOUNCED AT A LATER DATE. All interested parties must respond to any solicitation announcement separately from the responses to this announcement. title: Digitalt stoffkartotek
description: BESKRIVELSE AV LEVERANSEN (se vedlagte dokumenter for full beskrivelse) IKT Agder, som oppdragsgiver for denne konkurransen, gjennomfører en anskaffelse av en felles, skybasert løsning (SaaS) for digitalt stoffkartotek. Løsningen skal benyttes av Agder fylkeskommune, deltakende kommuner og øvrige virksomheter omfattet av anskaffelsen. Anskaffelsen skal bidra til bedre etterlevelse av lov- og forskriftskrav knyttet til håndtering av kjemi-kalier, styrke virksomhetenes arbeid med HMS og internkontroll, samt legge til rette for en mer stan-dardisert, effektiv og kostnadseffektiv forvaltning på tvers av de deltakende virksomhetene. Løsningen skal blant annet understøtte registrering og håndtering av kjemikalier, tilgang til og oppda-tering av sikkerhetsdatablader (SDS), risikovurderinger, eksponeringsregister, rapportering og rolle- og tilgangsstyring. Agder fylkeskommune kunngjør bare konkurransen på vegne av IKT-Agder som er oppdragsgiver.

title: Norway – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Digital substance register
description: DESCRIPTION OF THE DELIVERY (see the attached documents for a full description). ICT Agder, as the contracting authority for this competition, is carrying out a procurement of a joint, cloud based system (SaaS) for the digital substance register. The system shall be used by Agder county, participating municipalities and other entities included in the procurement. The procurement shall contribute to better compliance with legal and regulation requirements connected to handling chemistry calies, strengthen the entities ́ work with HSE and internal control, as well as facilitate a more stan-dardised, efficient and cost efficient management across the participating entities. The system shall, among other things, support registration and handling of chemicals, access to and monitoring safety data sheets (SDS), risk assessments, exposure register, reporting and role and access management. Agder county is only announcing the competition on behalf of ICT-Agder, the contracting authority.
